key_insight: Sparse, physically constrained model discovery can identify interpretable isotropic yield and failure surfaces, with sharp Lode-angle dependence more valuable than many additional terms.
engineering_relevance: The framework supports multiaxial material calibration while addressing physical admissibility and reducing nominal-stress mapping bias through differentiable finite-element identification.
method: Discover sparse invariant models enriched with cosine Lode-angle terms and learnable Podgorski–Bigoni–Piccolroaz atoms.
Combine convex gauge experts using physically motivated competition or direction gates with sparsity controls.
Fit through differentiable ray-wise first roots, enforcing library admissibility with penalties or competition-gate convexity by construction.
evidence_signal: Synthetic Mohr–Coulomb and PBP benchmarks achieved errors within 1%; five experimental datasets were analysed, with PBP atoms reducing concrete fitting error fourfold.
watch_item: For library models, convexity and absence of re-entrant branches are penalized rather than guaranteed, so fitted surfaces require admissibility checks.
paper_title: Sparse, admissible and interpretable: discovery of isotropic limit surfaces with extended invariant libraries, physically gated mixtures of experts, and end-to-end structural identification
